summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for App Services Values and Secrets; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: [low] A Value is a named reference to static data stored by Atlas that can be accessed in Atlas Functions, resolving to either plain text (JSON object, array, or string) or a Secret. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/functions/values.md
[low] You can access a Value's stored data from an Atlas Function using the context.values module. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/functions/values.md

[low] Value names cannot exceed 64 characters, must start with a letter or number, and may only contain ASCII letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/functions/values.md

[low] In previous MongoDB versions, Values and Secrets were distinct entities, allowing users to create secrets and link them to values. (verified as of 2026-10-15) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/using-secret-in-function-with-new-values-system/158875.json

[low] In newer MongoDB versions where secrets are values with a 'secret' type, users have reported inability to access newly created secrets in Realm functions. (verified as of 2026-10-15) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/using-secret-in-function-with-new-values-system/158875.json

[low] To link a secret to a value in the Mongo console, first create a 'secret', then create a 'value' and choose 'link' to that secret. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/using-secret-in-function-with-new-values-system/158875.json

[low] In a function, use context.values.get to retrieve the value, which in turn retrieves the linked secret. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/using-secret-in-function-with-new-values-system/158875.json
